meta.project: Integrated ESG-ABSA Intelligence Framework (v-1 to v3)
meta.description: Valid JSON artifact mapping research objective layers to contributions, research questions, and supporting literature evidence from the Thesis Evaluation and NAACL-2025 corpus.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Test-Time Code-Switching for Cross-lingual Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction
literature_references.authors: Dongming Sheng, Kexin Han, Hao Li, Yan Zhang, Yucheng Huang, Jun Lang, Wenqiang Liu
literature_references.relevance: Provides a generative framework for cross-lingual ASTE using code-switching, directly supporting C3 (cross-lingual transfer) and the foundational multilingual requirements of O1.

literature_references.title: Soft Language Prompts for Language Transfer
literature_references.authors: Ivan Vykopal, Simon Ostermann, Marián Simko
literature_references.relevance: Supports RQ1.1 by demonstrating how language-specific adapters and soft prompts improve transfer to mid- and low-resource languages, essential for Indonesian-English coverage.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: HMT: Hierarchical Memory Transformer for Efficient Long Context Language Processing
literature_references.authors: Zifan He, Yingqi Cao, Zongyue Qin, Neha Prakriya, Yizhou Sun, Jason Cong
literature_references.relevance: Validates C13 and RQ2.2 by proposing a memory-augmented hierarchy that processes long context with 2.5–116x less inference memory, directly addressing the scalability problems (P4) noted in the plan.

literature_references.title: MixLLM: Dynamic Routing in Mixed Large Language Models
literature_references.authors: Xinyu Wang, Yanchi Liu, Wei Cheng, Xujiang Zhao, Zhengzhang Chen, Wenchao Yu, Yanjie Fu, Haifeng Chen
literature_references.relevance: Provides a bandit-based routing system to assign queries to the most suitable LLM, supporting C10 and RQ2.4 by mitigating single-model bias and hallucinations through specialized selection.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: SymBa: Symbolic Backward Chaining for Structured Natural Language Reasoning
literature_references.relevance: Directly operationalizes C7 and RQ3.1 by integrating symbolic solvers with LLMs for backward-chaining proofs, creating the interpretable reasoning artifacts required by O3.

literature_references.title: Verify-in-the-Graph: Entity Disambiguation Enhancement for Complex Claim Verification with Interactive Graph Representation
literature_references.authors: Hoang Pham, Thanh-Do Nguyen, Khac-Hoai Nam Bui
literature_references.relevance: Provides evidence for C7 and RQ3.2, showing that structured triplet decomposition into graphs enables verifiable, deep sub-claim fact-checking.

research_questions: RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?
RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.2: How can cross-model consistency be measured?

literature_references.title: COVE: COntext and VEracity prediction for out-of-context images
literature_references.authors: Jonathan Tonglet, Gabriel Thiem, Iryna Gurevych
literature_references.relevance: Supports C11 and RQ4.5 by demonstrating a sequential process for context and veracity prediction, which mirrors the proposed narrative-grounded detection of greenwashing (H2/H5).

literature_references.title: Language Models Predict Empathy Gaps Between Social In-groups and Out-groups
literature_references.authors: Yu Hou, Hal Daum'e, Rachel Rudinger
literature_references.relevance: Addresses C14 and RQ4.1 by uncovering how model personas exhibit systematic biases based on identity cues, justifying the need for tone-aware correction and trust metrics.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: CSR-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Deployment of Computer Science Research Repositories
literature_references.authors: Yijia Xiao, Runhui Wang, Luyang Kong, Davor Golac, Wei Wang
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports O5 by providing an evaluation methodology for the autonomous deployment and audit of code repositories, essential for the open-source pipeline goals of C12.

literature_references.title: MICE for CATs: Model-Internal Confidence Estimation for Calibrating Agents with Tools
literature_references.authors: Nishant Subramani, Jason Eisner, Justin Svegliato, Benjamin Van Durme, Yu Su, Sam Thomson
